result.summary:
Independent gate of docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md, read in full directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). Given this role's two prior FAILs on the same code-vs-prose mistake (REQ-026, REQ-027), scanned exhaustively for it here first.

1. ZERO IMPLEMENTATION CODE CHECK (exhaustive). Enumerated every fenced code block in the document: Sec0 (CHECK constraint SQL, quoting an already-existing schema.ts constraint verbatim -- a citation of existing code, not new logic authored by this design), Sec2.1 (CheckinListItem interface + listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin signature -- bare, ends `;`), Sec2.2 (countCheckedIn signature -- bare), Sec3.1 (CheckinToggleDecisionInput/CheckinToggleOutcome types + decideCheckinToggleOutcome signature -- bare; the decision rule itself is stated as a first-match-wins TABLE, not an if/else body), Sec3.2 (toggleCheckIn signature -- bare; the 6-step sequence is numbered prose, not executable code, including the UPDATE/SELECT statements which are quoted as SQL text inside prose steps, not a function body), Sec4.1/4.2/4.3 (three handler function declarations, each `return async (ctx) => { ... }` -- ellipsis body, no logic), Sec4.2/4.3 (CHECKIN_TOGGLE_PATTERN / CHECKIN_PAGE_PATTERN regex constant declarations -- checked for precedent: docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md lines 480-481 already establish this exact convention, REMINDER24H_CONFIRM_PATTERN/REMINDER24H_DECLINE_PATTERN as regex constants, in a design that PASSED gate; this is a declarative callback_data-matching constant, not decision logic, same category as a type alias), Sec4.4 (CheckinListView interface + renderCheckinListMessage signature -- bare). Grepped the whole file for `if (`, `return <expr>;`, arithmetic assignment, `for`/`while` -- the only three hits are the three handler `return async (ctx) => { ... };` stub lines already accounted for above. displayName derivation, ordering rule, and the toggle decision rule are each stated as tables per this role's own established convention (code-designer.md's explicit instruction after the REQ-016/REQ-017 failures) -- verified no rule is smuggled back in as a one-line comparison. VERDICT: clean, no implementation code.

2. SCHEMA CLAIM VERIFIED BY DIRECT READ of apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts (not trusting the design's citation): line 256 `checkedInAt: timestamp("checked_in_at", ...)`, line 257-259 `checkedInBy: uuid("checked_in_by").references(() => users.id, { onDelete: "restrict" })`, line 260 `checkInMethod: checkInMethod("check_in_method")` with the enum defined at line 186 `pgEnum("check_in_method", ["qr", "manual"])`, and lines 296-297 the CHECK constraint `chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted` with body `${table.checkedInAt} IS NULL OR ${table.admission} = 'admitted'`. All three claims (two columns + the CHECK constraint) confirmed genuinely pre-existing, exactly as cited. No schema change needed; DATA-DESIGNER correctly not run.

3. S6 WRITE-TIME RECHECK TRACED RIGOROUSLY (AC1's crux) -- this is the check I gave the most scrutiny, per the task's instruction. Traced the full chain: (a) the toggle button's callback_data is `"checkin:toggle:" + registrationId` ONLY (Sec4.4, Sec1.4) -- no eventId, no admission, nothing else is ever encoded into it, and Sec1.4 gives the structural reason (64-byte budget: 15 + 36 = 51 bytes already consumes most of the budget, no room for a second UUID let alone an enum value); (b) toggleCheckIn (Sec3.2) opens `db.transaction`, and step 1's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` is stated to happen *inside* that transaction, reading `admission`/`checkedInAt` fresh from the row, explicitly 'never reusing any value the callback's own callback_data or the caller passed in'; (c) decideCheckinToggleOutcome (step 2) is called with exactly the fields just read from that SELECT -- registrationExists/admission/checkedInAt all sourced from the fresh row, none from any earlier render-time value; (d) the conditional UPDATE (steps 3-5) happens only after the decision, inside the same transaction, so the row remains locked from the SELECT through the UPDATE with no gap where a concurrent admission change could race in between decision and write. I looked specifically for whether the design's own optimizations (in-place keyboard edit after toggle, Sec1.5; eventId returned from toggleCheckIn for the handler's counter recompute, Sec3.2 step 6) reintroduce any admission value into callback_data or into any cross-call state -- they do not: eventId travels back to the handler as a return value from the SAME transactional call that just did the fresh read, not as an input the handler supplies, and no admission value is returned or reused anywhere. Sec3.3 additionally re-runs requireEventStaffForEvent at toggle time (S2 defense in depth), independent of and prior to the toggleCheckIn call, and does not affect or short-circuit the fresh SELECT. CONCLUSION: the design's structural argument holds -- the FOR UPDATE SELECT inside toggleCheckIn is genuinely the only place `admission` is read in the whole toggle path, there is no code path that could decide from a stale value, and the pre-existing DB CHECK constraint (verified in item 2) is a correctly-described independent second layer, not a substitute the design leans on to cover a gap in the first layer.

4. /checkin <event_id> [query] INTEGRATION WITH REQ-018 AUTHORIZATION (Sec4.1) -- traced step order: steps 1-6 (tgId extraction, lang, parse eventId+query, getEventById, endsAt check, requireEventStaffForEvent) are stated as unchanged from REQ-018 and run BEFORE step 7 (list render, first use of `query`). The parse in step 3 splits into eventId (first token) and query (remainder) but query is not read or dereferenced until step 7, strictly after the auth gate in step 6 has already returned ok. Query text cannot reach or alter the authorization check -- it is not passed to requireEventStaffForEvent, getEventById, or any argument of the auth path; it is used solely inside renderCheckinListMessage's item-filtering (Sec2.1), called only after authorization succeeds. No bypass path exists.

5. S3 PHONE/EMAIL EXCLUSION AT QUERY LEVEL -- confirmed Sec2.1 states the SELECT's field list explicitly ('Selects registrations.id, registrations.userId, registrations.checkedInAt, profiles.firstName, profiles.lastName, profiles.company, and ... users.tgUsername') and separately states 'Never selects profiles.phone or profiles.email -- this is what makes AC3 structurally true: those two columns are simply absent from this query's select clause, not filtered out after the fact.' This is a query-level exclusion (nothing to accidentally leak at render time because the columns are never fetched), matching the task's specific concern about display-time-only filtering bugs -- not applicable here since the columns never enter the result set.

6. LIVE COUNTER VERIFIED COMPUTED, NEVER STORED (AC4) -- Sec2.2's countCheckedIn is one `SELECT count(*)` re-run on every render path named explicitly (initial render Sec4.1, post-toggle header re-render Sec4.2 step 6, page turn Sec4.3). No new column proposed anywhere in the document, no cache, no in-memory counter -- confirmed by re-reading Sec9's 'reused unchanged' list and Sec0's schema table, neither adds a counter column. Denominator (total admitted) reuses listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin's already-fetched array length rather than a second count query -- correctly described as avoiding, not adding, a stored/cached value.

7. AUDIT LOG INTEGRATION -- exactly one writeAuditLog call per branch: Sec3.2 step 4 (`"registration.checkin"` action) for check-in, step 5 (`"registration.checkin_undo"` action) for undo -- two distinct action strings for the two distinct events, both inside the same transaction as their respective UPDATE (S8's 'exactly one row, same transaction' shape). The refusal branches (not-found, refused-not-admitted, step 3) explicitly write no audit row and no UPDATE, correctly matching AC1's 'no check-in written' wording (refusal is not itself a status change requiring its own audit row under S8's definition, and no AC asks for one).

8. ALL 6 ACs MAPPED (Sec8 table) -- AC1 (fresh locked SELECT + CHECK constraint + refusal alert), AC2 (check-in/undo UPDATE + exactly one audit row each), AC3 (query-level phone/email exclusion), AC4 (fresh count(*), no events-table write), AC5 (WHERE admission='admitted' at SQL layer), AC6 (command-argument search + substring filter + SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT=20 vs a >=10-attendee fixture) -- each row names a concrete section/mechanism, no AC left unaddressed, no TBD/deferral language found anywhere in the document (checked Sec6's 4 open questions individually -- each names a real residual gap with a reasoned accept/reject, not a placeholder for undone design work).

9. TOKENS -- Sec7 states no design-system token/component applies (bot has no visual/CSS surface); confirmed no color/spacing/typography reference appears anywhere in the document to check against docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css. Correct N/A, not a silent omission.

10. DISCOVERABILITY OPEN QUESTION (Sec1.3/Sec6 OQ3) -- JUDGMENT: acceptable, not a gate blocker. No acceptance criterion requires a persistent search UI; AC6 asks only that search narrow the list by name, which the command-argument pattern satisfies functionally. The rejected alternative (free-text follow-up requiring conversation state) is correctly rejected for a structural reason (S9's exact in-memory-state failure mode, or an unscoped schema change) rather than convenience. The footer hint (checkin.searchHint, restated on every render) is a real, if modest, mitigation, and Telegram's own UI (one-tap edit-and-resend of the prior command) reduces the practical friction below what the bare description suggests. This is the same category of accepted, explicitly-named residual UX gap the pipeline has already accepted at this gate for REQ-025/026/027 (a real limitation, named precisely, with the alternatives' costs stated) -- treating it as a hard blocker here would be inconsistent with that precedent and is not required by any AC. Recorded as a MINOR forward note, not a FAIL: product may eventually want a richer mechanism (a dedicated alias command, or genuine session-backed search once a session mechanism exists for other reasons), but that is correctly left to a future requirement rather than silently resolved or over-built here.

Verdict: PASS. All Step 1b checks (2a-2d) satisfied for every AC; schema claim verified true by direct read; S6 write-time recheck traced end-to-end and holds structurally; REQ-018 authorization integration correctly ordered; S3 exclusion is query-level; live counter genuinely computed; audit log correct; discoverability open question is an acceptable, adequately-justified residual gap, not a defect.

context.verification_notes: Schema claim (checked_in_by, check_in_method, chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted) independently re-verified against apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts lines 186, 256-260, 296-298 -- all confirmed genuinely pre-existing, not taken on the design's word. Regex PATTERN-constant convention cross-checked against docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md lines 480-481 (a passed prior design) as precedent for declarative callback_data-matching constants not counting as implementation code.
